result.summary:
Scope test: this diff touches partition DDL against tenant schemas (8 new migrations, all `if prefix() do`-guarded) and extends EventStore.read/2 to union events + events_archive for replay -- a tenant-data path per the applicability notes. Did NOT take the out-of-scope shortcut; ran the full INV-1..INV-9 assessment against `git diff main...HEAD`, independently (read the actual diff for lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex in full, lib/letflow/event_store.ex, lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex, lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, and all 8 migration files in full), not from ELIXIR-DEV's handoff summary alone.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES (S1 done, S2 migrations exist, per security-invariants.md's 2026-08-17 addendum; live now, not a default skip). (a) Every new query/DDL statement is scoped through the tenant schema: PartitionMaintenance's functions all take `schema_name` and interpolate it (never any other identifier) into every statement's schema-qualifier; EventStore.read/2's new archived_events query uses `Repo.all(prefix: schema_name)` identically to the pre-existing live_events query, same :prefix mechanism. (b) All 8 migrations are wrapped in `if prefix() do ... end` (confirmed by reading each file) and all 8 are registered in Letflow.TenantProvisioning.@tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (confirmed in the tenant_provisioning.ex diff) -- none reachable outside the tenant-scoped mechanism, none left in public. (c) Neither `events` nor `events_archive` (nor their new partitioned/archived-child tables) carries a tenant_id column at all in this diff -- scoping is 100% via schema :prefix, consistent with 0003's mechanism; no caller-supplied tenant_id field is introduced anywhere. PASS.

INV-2, INV-3, INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No client-facing API response type is touched (INV-2, S4 not started), no scripting/plugin sandbox is touched (INV-3, S5 not started), no lookup-by-ID endpoint is touched (INV-5, S4 not started). retire_month/3 is a plain Elixir function with no HTTP-facing caller in this diff.

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES (live). Ran `grep -rniE "(password|secret|client_secret|token)\s*(=|:)\s*\"[^\"]{8,}\""` over every changed lib/ and priv/repo/migrations/ file in this diff: zero hits. No secret material of any kind is introduced, logged, or threaded through this diff. PASS.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES, satisfied by this handoff itself (the meta-invariant).

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation of tenant/user-controlled data) -- APPLIES (live), the invariant this diff most heavily exercises. Read every `Repo.query!`/`execute` call site in partition_maintenance.ex and all 8 migrations. Two interpolation classes:
  (1) Identifiers (schema/table/index/constraint/sequence names) -- unavoidably interpolated (SQL has no bind-parameter syntax for identifiers). Every schema identifier used is either `schema_name` (validated at function entry via `TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1`'s `"tenant_" <> 32-lowercase-hex` shape+UUID-cast check before any query fires -- confirmed in tenant_provisioning.ex:241-256) or `prefix()` in migrations (the migration runner's own resolved tenant schema, never request/param input). Table/index/constraint/sequence name fragments are 100% fixed string literals (`events`, `events_archive`, `events_default`, `events_archive_default`, `uq_event_sequence_p`, etc.) or built via `partition_name/3` / `bounds_constraint_name/2` from `year`/`month`, which are typed integers (`year :: pos_integer()`, `month :: 1..12` guard clauses in retire_month/3's own function head; ensure_future_partitions derives them internally from `Date.utc_today()` + integer offsets, never from caller-supplied strings) -- no free-text ever reaches an identifier position.
  (2) Partition-bound DDL literals (`FOR VALUES FROM/TO`, `CHECK (...)` bounds) -- confirmed these are inline string-interpolated rather than bound parameters, and confirmed this is a genuine Postgres restriction, not a shortcut: FOR VALUES/CHECK-bound clauses in DDL are constant-expression-only and Postgres/Postgrex rejects a parameterized form outright (documented at the exact call sites, e.g. partition_maintenance.ex:184-193, and independently in every migration's own comments). The interpolated `from_bound`/`to_bound` values are always the output of `month_bounds/2`, built purely from the same validated `year`/`month` integers -- never from any other source. Verified this holds for ALL of: create_partition!/5, ensure_bounds_constraint!/5, attach_partition!/4 in partition_maintenance.ex, and the equivalent helpers in migrations 2 and 6.
  Every genuine DML value (event_id lists, created_at lists, batch limits, month bounds used in an ordinary SELECT/WHERE) IS passed as a real Postgrex bind parameter ($1/$2/$3) -- confirmed in do_reconcile_default_partition_loop/6, relocate_default_batch!/3, relocate_protected_rows/2, child_of?/3, pending_detach?/2, constraint_exists?/3, column_exists?/3, default_partition_attached?/1. No hit found anywhere of tenant- or user-controlled free text reaching a raw SQL string. PASS.

Cross-tenant-leakage check (part of INV-1/INV-7 verification): every DDL/DML statement in the new module and all 8 migrations is schema-qualified to exactly one `schema_name`/`prefix()` per call -- no statement iterates or acts across multiple tenant schemas at once (ensure_future_partitions/2 and retire_month/3 both operate on exactly the one schema_name passed in; the Poller's per-tenant fan-out in maybe_run_partition_maintenance/2 calls run_partition_maintenance_sweep once per schema via the pre-existing fetch_tenant_schemas()/run_sweep per-tenant iteration pattern already used identically by every other existing sweep -- schema_name reaching PartitionMaintenance is therefore always system-derived from TenantProvisioning's own tenant registry, never client/request input). No cross-tenant leakage risk found.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES (live) for the path actually wired to a runtime caller in this diff: ensure_future_partitions/2, reached via Letflow.Scheduler.run_partition_maintenance_sweep/1 from Poller's maybe_run_partition_maintenance/2. Confirmed this path IS isolated: run_partition_maintenance_sweep/1 rescues Postgrex.Error for :undefined_table/:undefined_schema explicitly (schema mid-deprovision), reraising anything else; that reraise is in turn caught per-schema inside run_sweep's Task.async_stream fan-out (the same try/rescue -> log_task_raise pattern every other existing sweep in poller.ex already uses) -- an unexpected DB error for one tenant's sweep cannot crash the Poller process or affect other tenants' concurrent tasks in the same tick. This is the existing, already-reviewed isolation shape, not a new pattern. retire_month/3, by contrast, uses Repo.query!/1,2 (raising) throughout with no caller anywhere in this diff (not wired to Scheduler/Poller or any other entry point -- confirmed by grep, only test/design-doc references exist) -- so it is not currently reachable from external I/O, tenant input, or network input at all, and INV-8 has nothing to apply to on that function yet. ELIXIR-DEV already flagged this honestly as MINOR for REVIEWER (idiom/consistency, not reachability) rather than concealing it -- correct call, does not block this gate. PASS as applied to the actually-reachable path; the MINOR note carries forward, not a BLOCKER.

INV-9 (tenant-controlled outbound URL validation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No outbound HTTP request of any kind is touched by this diff.

Independent assessment of ELIXIR-DEV's two flagged MAJOR design deviations, for security-invariant consequence specifically (not idiom/architecture soundness, which is REVIEWER's call at 2d):
  (a) events_default temporary detach/reattach around DETACH PARTITION ... CONCURRENTLY. Confirmed this operates only on `"#{schema_name}".events` for the one tenant schema passed to retire_month/3 -- no cross-tenant reach, and the detach/reattach pair is idempotent and self-healing exactly as described (verified ensure_default_partition_detached!/1 and ensure_default_partition_reattached!/1 both check catalog state via pg_inherits before acting, and reattach is unconditionally called at the top of every retire_month/3 call). The stated trade-off (a write outside every pre-created partition's range failing during the brief window instead of being caught by the default-partition safety net) is an availability/robustness question for one tenant's own writes during that tenant's own retirement call -- it does not create a tenant-isolation violation, a SQL-injection surface, a secret-exposure path, or a crash reachable from another tenant's traffic (retire_month/3 is not currently wired to any caller, so this window is not live in production yet regardless). No INV violated; correctly routed to REVIEWER for the architecture trade-off call, not a SECURITY-REVIEWER blocker.
  (b) ensure_archived_at_column!/1's fast-default archived_at column addition before ATTACH. Checked whether the constant-literal default could leak into read/2's results incorrectly: confirmed archived_event_to_event/1 (event_store.ex) builds the %Event{} struct explicitly field-by-field and does NOT include archived_at at all -- the synthetic default timestamp on a moved-in-place partition's archived_at column can never surface through EventStore.read/2's output, for any tenant. Checked the race question (two retire_month/3 calls for different months): each call's ADD COLUMN targets a distinct, month-specific partition table (`events_y<year>m<month>`), never the shared parent, so two different months' calls do not contend on the same relation for this step; the only shared-object contention is the brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE Postgres takes on the `events_archive` parent during each call's own ATTACH PARTITION step, which Postgres itself serializes safely (a blocking/performance question, not a data-integrity or tenant-isolation one) -- and again, retire_month/3 has no live caller in this diff, so concurrent retirement isn't actually possible yet. No INV violated; correctly routed to REVIEWER.

Overall: no applicable invariant failed. All BLOCKER-severity checks that apply today (INV-1, INV-4, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8-as-reachable) pass on independent re-derivation from the actual diff, not from ELIXIR-DEV's self-report.
result.next_action: Route to REVIEWER (2d) -- REVIEWER must assess the two MAJOR design deviations ELIXIR-DEV flagged (events_default self-heal detach/reattach; archived_at fast-default column before ATTACH) for architecture/idiom soundness and decide whether decision 0037/the design doc need amending, plus the MINOR Repo.query!/typed-tuple consistency note on PartitionMaintenance -- none of these are security-invariant failures, all are within REVIEWER's remit.
